item.mechanism: Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between phases, alleviating stress concentration and enabling synergistic deformation, which prevents interfacial cracking.
item.system: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi (Ho alloy) treated at 6 GPa and 1473 K
item.operating_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature; HPHT treatment at 6 GPa, 1473 K for 2 h
item.supporting_observation: TEM and ECCI showed dislocations extending across coherent interfaces and a mismatch factor of 0.004, contrasting with incoherent interfaces in untreated alloys.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold for untreated eutectic high entropy alloys with incoherent interfaces where strain localization and interfacial cracking occur.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional hot isostatic pressing and thermal-mechanical treatments which did not produce the same strength-ductility synergy.
quotes: The coherent interface holds a key to the activation of the multiple deformation mechanisms
Dislocations preferentially initiate in the softer FCC phase, and subsequently are allowed to transfer into the harder B2 phase due to the highly coherent interface
Such coherent FCC/B2 interface in the HPHT-treated alloy is clearly distinguished from the corresponding interface in the Ho alloy

item.mechanism: Hierarchically patterned microstructure promotes strain delocalization by allowing multiple deformation mechanisms (dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, twins) to activate at multiple length scales.
item.system: HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy with hexagonal-like structural units
item.operating_conditions: Plastic deformation up to 35% strain at room temperature
item.supporting_observation: ECCI and TEM revealed progressive activation of stacking faults, microbands, and deformation twins in both FCC and B2 phases, leading to homogeneous KAM distribution.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism relies on the specific hierarchically patterned structure; not observed in the Ho alloy where B2 phase shows limited dislocation activity.
item.alternatives_considered: Localized deformation at interfaces and absence of dislocation in the BCC phase observed in the Ho alloy.
quotes: Such strength-ductility synergy is attributed to the HPHT-induced formation of a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces, which promotes multiple deformation mechanisms
The increased misorientation distribution of FCC and B2 phases with increasing strain also indicates strain delocalization in the tensile-deformed HPHT-treated alloy
Such progressive activation of multiple plastic deformation mechanisms in both FCC and BCC phases of the HPHT alloy is in distinct contrast to the case of Ho alloy

item.mechanism: High-density dislocation storage and compatible strain distribution between FCC and B2 phases prevent premature plastic instability and enhance work hardening.
item.operating_conditions: Tensile loading from 0% to 35% strain at room temperature
item.supporting_observation: GND density increased rapidly in both phases, reaching identical values at 35% strain, unlike the Ho alloy where severe mismatch occurred.
item.scope_limits: Requires the specific coherent interface structure; incompatible plastic strain distribution leads to failure in the untreated Ho alloy.
item.alternatives_considered: Severe mismatch in GND density between phases in the Ho alloy indicating highly incompatible plastic strain distribution.
quotes: Upon further loading, the GND density of the B2 phase increases much faster than that of the FCC phase, eventually resulting in an identical value of GND density in both phases at 35% strain
The differences among strain-hardening rate curves strongly indicate the different deformation behaviors of these alloys during plastic deformation
Moreover, the GND densities in the HPHT alloy are much higher than those in the Ho alloy, indicating improved capability of dislocation storage in the HPHT-treated alloy

item.mechanism: Deformation twins and microbands act as barriers to dislocation motion and pin refined microbands, promoting mutual interactions and further strain hardening.
item.system: HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy deformed to 35% strain
item.operating_conditions: High plastic strain (35%) at room temperature
item.supporting_observation: ECCI and TEM images showed intersected deformation twins and microbands extending across phases, which were absent in the Ho alloy.
item.scope_limits: Twins are activated only at later stages of deformation when interface coherency decays; not observed in the Ho alloy at fracture.
item.alternatives_considered: Only limited slip lines in FCC phase and no evident dislocation activities in BCC phase in the Ho alloy.
quotes: More interestingly, we observed clear traits of deformation twins (DTs) in the highly deformed hierarchically patterned structure
At a later stage of deformation, as the coherency of the FCC/B2 interfaces decays, deformation twins are activated to further accommodate deformation
Note that neither HDDWs nor DTs were observed in the Ho alloy at fracture

item.mechanism: Isolated microcracks and unbroken ligaments near the fracture surface shield crack propagation and prevent coalescence into elongated voids.
item.system: HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy after tensile fracture
item.supporting_observation: SEM showed high density of isolated microcracks cutting through B2 phase and twisted fracture paths, contrasting with elongated cracks in the Ho alloy.
item.scope_limits: Contrasts with the catastrophic fracture mode in conventional eutectic high entropy alloys where elongated cracks form along interfaces.
item.alternatives_considered: Elongated cracks with large width along the interfaces in the fractured Ho alloy leading to catastrophic damage.
quotes: Isolated microcracks are uniformly distributed near the fracture surface in the HPHT-treated samples, in contrast to the catastrophic fracture in those without HPHT treatment
Numerous isolated microcracks cut through the B2 phase and the fracture paths were twisted among the two phases in the HPHT-treated alloy, preventing crack coalescing into elongated voids
Besides, a number of unbroken ligaments were observed near the fracture surface, which is believed to shield crack propagation

item.mechanism: Stacking faults near interfaces accommodate local interfacial stresses, serving as an early mechanism for stress relief before microband formation.
item.system: HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy at 5% and 15% strain
item.operating_conditions: Low to moderate plastic strain (5% to 15%) at room temperature
item.supporting_observation: ECCI identified extended stacking faults near interfaces at 5% strain, with density increasing at 15% strain.
item.scope_limits: Observed primarily in the early stages of deformation; not the dominant mechanism at high strains where twins and microbands prevail.
item.alternatives_considered: Localized deformation at the interface observed in the Ho alloy where stacking faults were not the primary accommodation mechanism.
quotes: Formation of extended stacking faults (SFs) near the interfaces is also identified, which has been regarded as a mechanism that accommodates local interfacial stresses
With strain increasing to 15%, SFs are activated in the FCC phase with a much higher density as compared with those at 5% strain

item.mechanism: The HPHT treatment modifies the microstructure to a hierarchically patterned structure with coherent interfaces, which is inaccessible to conventional processing techniques.
item.system: Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy processed via HPHT at 6 GPa, 1473 K
item.operating_conditions: HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 h
item.supporting_observation: EBSD and TEM confirmed the transformation from dual-phase lamellae to hexagonal-like structural units with coherent interfaces, while phase constitution remained unchanged.
item.scope_limits: Conventional hot isostatic pressing and thermal-mechanical treatments did not produce this specific microstructure or the resulting mechanical synergy.
item.alternatives_considered: Conventional hot isostatic pressing treatment and thermal-mechanical treatment which failed to achieve the same strength-ductility synergy.
quotes: Such strength-ductility synergy is attributed to the HPHT-induced formation of a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces

The hierarchically patterned structure with coherent interfaces modulated through HPHT treatment is expected to have a major impact on the mechanical response of the HPHT-treated alloy, which is generally inaccessible to conventional materials processing techniques

item.mechanism: The HPHT strategy is generally applicable to other alloy systems and pure metals to achieve similar strength-ductility improvements.
item.system: Pure metal copper and other unspecified alloy systems
item.operating_conditions: HPHT treatment using a self-designed hexahedron-anvil-press apparatus
item.supporting_observation: Authors state the strategy can be extended to pure metal copper and other alloy systems based on the adjustable parameters of the apparatus.
item.scope_limits: Specific results for other alloys are not detailed in the main text, only referenced in supplementary figures.
item.alternatives_considered: None explicitly stated as alternatives for other systems, but implies conventional methods are insufficient.
quotes: We further demonstrate that the HPHT treatment can be easily extended to other alloy systems for synergistic improvement of strength and ductility
These findings suggest a new direction of research in employing HPHT techniques to help develop next generation structural materials
